# DuplexJev-32B-Para (v1.3)

📄 Paper: [arXiv:2610.02638](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02638) · Code: [github.com/adventists-ai/duplexjev](https://github.com/adventists-ai/duplexjev) · Research notes: [hearing stress](https://github.com/adventists-ai/duplexjev/blob/main/research/2026-10-stress-understanding.md) · [keeping a speech-decision LLM able to talk](https://github.com/adventists-ai/duplexjev/blob/main/research/2026-10-chat-replay.md)

**The DuplexJev model that hears the most beyond the words.** On top of everything
[DuplexJev-32B-Turn](https://huggingface.co/adventists-ai/DuplexJev-32B-Turn) and
[DuplexJev-32B-Stress](https://huggingface.co/adventists-ai/DuplexJev-32B-Stress) do (spoken QA, gender, emotion,
turn-taking, stress and pauses), it also hears **laughter, breathing, coughs and sighs**, notices **how** someone is
talking (whispering, shouting, very fast or slow), and can tell, roughly as a person would, **whether two clips are
the same speaker**. Mandarin and English. Since v1.1 it also **holds a normal conversation**, multi-turn included.
**v1.2** adds **accent judgments** (English accents and Mandarin dialect regions) and much sharper **end-of-turn
detection right after the user pauses**: on LiveKit's eot-bench it now beats Smart Turn v3.2 in English and Chinese.
**v1.3** hears **stress** much better: on the public StressTest benchmark it goes from 72 to **85**, on StressPresso's
meaning questions from 69 to **89**, and on choosing the meaning a stressed word implies (DEBATE, held-out) from 85 to **93**, with the
other decisions about the same.

> **v1.3 (2026-10-15)** replaces v1.2 (2026-10-13): stress and pauses are much better, emotion is a little better,
> gender and Easy-Turn are about one point lower (table below).
> Earlier versions stay available as revisions `v1.2`, `v1.1` and `v1.0` (`--revision v1.2` in vLLM, `revision="v1.2"`
> in `from_pretrained`).

DuplexJev reads typed, closed-set decisions from speech as a **single-token distribution** of the LLM: zero decode
steps, many questions about the same clip in parallel. This repository is the complete model (Qwen3-ASR-0.6B encoder
+ connector + the language model of Qwen3-VL-32B, 33.0 B parameters, bf16; one 80 GB GPU).

**Which 32B to pick.** This one, for everything above, including live turn-taking and stress.

## What changed

Starting from DuplexJev-32B-Turn we trained the connector and a new rank-16 LoRA on the LLM (merged here) for 4,000
steps. The mix is the 32B-Turn mix plus:

| added data | what it teaches |
|---|---|
| stress / pause detection (as in 32B-Stress: DEBATE, Stress-17K, TinyStress-15K, Expresso, neutral negatives) | which word is stressed, or none; where the pause is |
| speaker pairs (VoxCeleb1 dev, AISHELL-1, LibriSpeech, two-speaker mixtures) | same speaker or not; is this person in the clip |
| non-verbal sounds (VocalSound, NonVerbalSpeech-38K, NonverbalTTS, Expresso laughing) | is there laughter / breathing / a cough / a sigh / sniffing / throat clearing / a sneeze / crying …; negatives are cut from the same recordings away from the event |
| speaking style (EARS, Expresso whisper) | whispering, loud, fast, slow, high or low pitch, normal |
| spoken multiple-choice replay (ARC, OpenBookQA and CommonsenseQA train splits read by TTS) | keeps "answer the content" from being crowded out by "listen to the voice" |
| **v1.1:** conversation replay (spoken and typed user turns, up to 6 earlier turns as history; target = the original LLM's own reply) and in-house chat items | normal, full-length replies; trained with per-row loss averaging so long replies do not swamp the one-token decisions |
| **v1.2:** accents (VCTK, English Dialects, EdAcc, Common Voice accent labels, KeSpeech; held-out speakers kept for testing) | which accent: 19 English accents and 9 Mandarin dialect regions; native speaker or not; standard Mandarin or not; which English region |
| **v1.2:** end of turn right after a pause (otoSpeech-141h cut 0.2 s into each pause, with DualTurn labels; Smart Turn v3.2 training set) | finished vs. still talking / hesitating when the user has just gone quiet, the way a live voice agent has to decide |
| **v1.3:** the stress data re-balanced (more "which meaning does this stress imply" items, weight raised) and the gender data weighted ×2; no new corpora | choosing the meaning a stressed word implies; keeping gender where it was |

| which word is stressed, "none" offered: DEBATE (zh) / StressPresso (en) | 35 / 1 | 93 / 96 | 92 / 91 | **95 / 96** |
| neutral speech → "no word is stressed": AISHELL-1 / LibriSpeech | 92 / 50 | 100 / 99 | 99 / — | 98 / 83 |

## Turn-taking benchmarks (v1.2 / v1.3)

**LiveKit [eot-bench](https://github.com/livekit/eot-bench)** (validation set, decision 0.2 s into each pause, official
metrics). False cut-offs when the agent may wait at most 300 / 600 ms (lower is better):

| | English | Chinese |
|---|---:|---:|
| LiveKit Turn Detector v1 | 9.9 / 4.5% | 20.6 / 8.7% |
| **DuplexJev-32B-Para v1.2, with the assistant's previous message** (plugin default, full eot-bench run) | **20.0 / 9.4%** | **37.7 / 12.2%** |
| DuplexJev-32B-Para v1.2, with the assistant's previous message, `readout="act"` (fast mode) | 18.4 / 7.9% | 37.3 / 12.3% |
| DuplexJev-32B-Para v1.2, audio only (fast mode) | 23.5 / 11.1% | 40.0 / 12.8% |
| **DuplexJev-32B-Para v1.3, with the assistant's previous message** (fast mode) | 20.3 / 8.8% | **35.5** / 12.3% |
| DuplexJev-32B-Para v1.3, audio only (fast mode) | 24.7 / 11.2% | 38.8 / 12.0% |
| DuplexJev-32B-Turn, audio only (fast mode) | 29.8 / 13.9% | 44.9 / 14.5% |
| Smart Turn v3.2 | 35.2 / 14.8% | 42.9 / 13.2% |

eot-bench audio is not in our training data. "With the assistant's previous message" puts
`The assistant had just said: "..."` before the audio; the Pipecat and LiveKit plugins send it
(`pipecat-duplexjev>=0.3`, `livekit-plugins-duplexjev>=0.2`, gateway `duplexjev>=0.6`). Plugin default: the turn
question, P(finished) + P(backchannel); run with every eot-bench decision point (adapter
`benchmarks/turn_detection/eot_bench/duplexjev_ctx_adapter.py` on GitHub). `readout="act"` (`pipecat-duplexjev>=0.4`,
`livekit-plugins-duplexjev>=0.3`): question "What should the assistant do now?", P(reply now) + P(short
acknowledgement). Rows marked fast mode ask once per pause, at the 0.2 s score point.

**Pipecat [Smart Turn v3.2](https://huggingface.co/datasets/pipecat-ai/smart-turn-data-v3.2-test) test set**
(accuracy at threshold 0.5): v1.2 English 94.0% (Smart Turn v3.2: 94.7%), Chinese 91.1% (90.5%); v1.3 94.2% / 91.4%; DuplexJev-32B-Turn
65.2% / 84.6%. The Smart Turn v3.2 *training* set is in our training mix, so this is an in-distribution result.

## Serve with vLLM

```bash
pip install "vllm[audio]>=0.29" duplexjev-vllm
vllm serve adventists-ai/DuplexJev-32B-Para --max-model-len 4096
```

Prompt format and client are the same as for [DuplexJev-32B-Turn](https://huggingface.co/adventists-ai/DuplexJev-32B-Turn);
see [`examples/vllm_client.py`](https://github.com/adventists-ai/duplexjev/blob/main/examples/vllm_client.py). Examples:

```
The user said: <|audio|>

Is there laughter in this audio?

Options:
A. Yes
B. No

Answer with the letter only.
```

```
用户说：<|audio|>

除了说话，这段音频里还有哪种声音？

选项：
A. 叹气
B. 咳嗽
C. 笑声
D. 都没有

请只回答选项字母。
```

Always offer a "none" option for stress and non-verbal questions; the model was trained with it.

## Limitations

- Non-verbal training audio is mostly acted (radio drama, animation, studio recordings); in natural conversation the
  scores are lower (see the table).
- Breathing in natural Mandarin conversation is weak (AUC 0.56 in v1.2, 0.65 in v1.1, 0.78 in v1.0); acted / read
  speech is much better.
- v1.2 is a little lower than v1.1 on English stress-word detection, sighs and same-speaker pairs; v1.3 brings the
  stress scores back up. v1.3 is about one point lower than v1.2 on gender and Easy-Turn, and four points lower on
  "standard Mandarin or not" across corpora (160 items).
- StressTest: 85 on the full public set; Gemini 3.8 Flash scores higher (89 on our 200-item sample).
- Accent answers describe how someone sounds, not where they are from or who they are; accents are often mixed or
  ambiguous. Do not use them to make decisions about people.
- Asked about itself, it may describe abilities (seeing images, speaking) that this checkpoint does not have on its
  own: it takes speech and text and replies in text.
- Speaker judgments are coarse (EER 18–40%) and must not be used to identify or verify people.
- Emotion labels come from acted corpora; do not use the outputs to make decisions about individuals.

Nodes on GitHub · All samples · Qwen3-ASR for the transcripts · The original model

**[Fish Audio Drama 3](https://huggingface.co/fishaudio/drama-3)**, converted for the native ComfyUI nodes of **[ComfyUI-Drama3](https://github.com/PedroMarinhoDev/ComfyUI-Drama3)**: a 35B text-to-speech model for voice cloning, dialogue and inline cues such as `[sighs]` or `[whispers]`, running **on cards from 8 GB**. 90% of the model is routed experts and each audio frame uses only 8 of the 256 in a layer, so the nodes keep the experts in system RAM and a cache of the ones in use on the GPU. Each file holds the whole model in one file; the codec is separate. Built with Fish Audio. ## Samples No real person is cloned here: the first three clone voices the model made up from a single line, the rest are voices it invents from the prompt alone. Drama 3 FP8, experts in RAM, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.9, top_k 30. **[More on the demo page →](https://pedromarinhodev.github.io/ComfyUI-Drama3/)** **Voice cloning**: the source clip, a voice the model made up from one line, then a new line in that voice > The lighthouse keeper climbed the last step, set her lantern on the sill, and watched the storm roll in across the bay. Somewhere below, a bell began to ring. **Inline cues** > [whispers] Don't move. I think it heard us. [pause] [sighs] Oh, it's only the cat. [laughs] You should have seen your face. **Two speakers** > <|speaker:0|> Did you remember the tickets?
> <|speaker:1|> [laughs] I thought you had them!
> <|speaker:0|> [sighs] Then we're watching the concert from the parking lot. **Five speakers**, no voices given: the model casts all five > <|speaker:0|> [dramatic dungeon master] You enter the dark cave. A dragon sleeps on a pile of gold.
> <|speaker:1|> [brave, too loud] I attack the dragon! … **Singing** > [singing, grand operatic] Oh toast, my golden toast, you're the bread I love the most! [singing softly] Crispy edges, warm and brown, finest slice in all the town. … **Portuguese** > [Brazilian football fan, building tension, Portuguese] Vai, vai, vai, vai! Ele passou por um, passou por dois, [shouting] olha o chute! … ## Files **Start with FP8**: it holds Fish Audio's own expert weights, byte for byte, next to the checkpoint's bf16 layers. The int8 file is the same size, measured as close to the original, and ran 14–17% faster than FP8 on an RTX 3090: the nodes turn FP8 experts into bf16 each time they run, while int8 experts run as int8. Take a smaller file when your system RAM is short of the FP8 file's ~48 GB. Every model file needs the codec. | File | Size | Experts | System RAM | Notes | |---|---|---|---|---| | [`drama3_fp8experts_bf16.safetensors`](drama3_fp8experts_bf16.safetensors) | 38.6 GB | FP8, as Fish Audio ships them | ~48 GB | the original weights | | [`drama3_int8experts_bf16.safetensors`](drama3_int8experts_bf16.safetensors) | 38.7 GB | int8 ConvRot | ~48 GB | faster than FP8 on the 3090; no silent take in 12 cloned test takes | | [`drama3_w6a8experts_bf16.safetensors`](drama3_w6a8experts_bf16.safetensors) | 32.7 GB | W6A8 | ~40 GB | no silent take in 16 cloned test takes | | [`drama3_w4a8experts_bf16.safetensors`](drama3_w4a8experts_bf16.safetensors) | 24.6 GB | W4A8 | ~32 GB | falls silent more often with real voice clips | | [`drama3_codec.safetensors`](drama3_codec.safetensors) | 1.6 GB | | | the original codec, fp32 | ## Quick start 1. **Install the nodes**: clone [ComfyUI-Drama3](https://github.com/PedroMarinhoDev/ComfyUI-Drama3) into `ComfyUI/custom_nodes` and restart ComfyUI. # IndexTTS-2.5

IndexTTS-2.5 is a zero-shot text-to-speech model that clones a voice from a single
reference audio clip. It supports **Chinese, English, Japanese, Spanish and Arabic**,
with cross-lingual voice transfer and emotion control disentangled from timbre.

Compared with IndexTTS-2, it adds Japanese, Spanish and Arabic, infers faster, adds
speaking speed control, and improves controllability of Chinese Pinyin, English CMU
phonemes and Japanese Kana.

## Model Details

- **Developed by:** IndexTeam, Bilibili
- **Model type:** Autoregressive zero-shot TTS — GPT backbone, flow-matching
  speech-to-mel decoder, BigVGAN vocoder
- **Parameters:** ~0.8B (GPT backbone)
- **Languages:** Chinese, English, Japanese, Spanish, Arabic
- **Output:** 22.05 kHz waveform
- **License:** [bilibili Model Use License Agreement](LICENSE)
- **Repository:** [github.com/index-tts/index-tts](https://github.com/index-tts/index-tts)
- **Paper:** [arXiv:2601.03888](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.03888)

## Getting Started

Requires Python 3.10–3.11, an NVIDIA GPU, and roughly 6 GB of VRAM for inference.

### Install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/index-tts/index-tts.git && cd index-tts
pip install -U uv
uv sync --all-extras
```

### Download the weights

```bash
# HuggingFace
uv tool install "huggingface-hub"
hf download IndexTeam/IndexTTS-2.5 --local-dir=checkpoints

# or ModelScope
uv tool install "modelscope"
modelscope download --model IndexTeam/IndexTTS-2.5 --local_dir checkpoints
```

Auxiliary models (w2v-bert-2.0, MaskGCT semantic codec, CAMPPlus, BigVGAN) are not
part of this repository; they are downloaded into `checkpoints/hf_cache/` on first run.

### Inference

```python
from indextts.infer_v2_5 import IndexTTS2

tts = IndexTTS2(cfg_path="checkpoints/config.yaml", model_dir="checkpoints", use_bf16=True)

# Voice cloning
tts.infer(
    spk_audio_prompt="prompt.wav",
    text="Hello, this is a voice cloning demo.",
    lang="EN",
    output_path="output.wav",
)

# Emotion control with an 8-float vector, in the order
# [happy, angry, sad, afraid, disgusted, melancholic, surprised, calm]
tts.infer(
    spk_audio_prompt="prompt.wav",
    text="快躲起来！是他要来了！",
    lang="ZH",
    output_path="output.wav",
    emo_vector=[0, 0, 0.8, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0],
)

# Pronunciation control: Pinyin, CMU phonemes, or Kana in <word|reading> form
tts.infer(
    spk_audio_prompt="prompt.wav",
    text="他在银<行|XING2>里<行|HANG2>走了半天。",
    lang="ZH",
    output_path="output.wav",
)

# Speaking speed: >1.0 slows down, <1.0 speeds up (valid range 0.5–2.0)
tts.infer(
    spk_audio_prompt="prompt.wav",
    text="大家好，欢迎来到IndexTTS。",
    lang="ZH",
    output_path="output.wav",
    duration_factor=1.2,
)
```

### Web UI

```bash
uv run webui.py
```

## Limitations

- Long text is split into segments and the pieces are concatenated with a short
  silence, so prosody is not modelled across a segment boundary.
- Emotion control from a text description needs the QwenEmotion model, which is
  loaded only when IndexTTS2 is constructed with `use_qwen_emo=True`. Passing
  `use_emo_text=True` without it raises at inference time.
- Enabling random sampling for emotion (`use_random=True`) reduces voice cloning
  fidelity.
- The model does not verify that the speaker in a reference clip consented to being
  cloned. Obtaining that consent is the user's responsibility, and all use is subject
  to the license terms.

# Shtorm-PocketTTS-RU v2 «версия 2, 01.10.2026»

Русская модель для [pocket-tts](https://github.com/kyutai-labs/pocket-tts) (Kyutai),
заточенная под **чтение книг**: ровная книжная подача, живая интонация,
клонирование голоса по короткому рефу.

> Запускайте по примеру из раздела [Запуск](#запуск). Автоматический пример в кнопке
> «Use this model» использует английский текст и английский голос — латиница моделью
> пока не поддерживается.

- архитектура оригинального pocket-tts: 6 слоёв, ~100M параметров — быстро и на CPU;
- токенизатор SentencePiece на русском корпусе (4000 токенов), общий для обеих моделей.

## Две модели: fast и slow

Разница в подаче, а не в качестве:

- **fast** (`config_fast.yaml`, он же `config.yaml`) — бодрее и живее: шире интонация,
  медленные голоса не тянут. На быстрых голосах может строчить.
- **slow** (`config_slow.yaml`) — спокойнее: свободнее паузы, ровнее тон.
  На медленных голосах может тянуть.

На одной и той же главе разница около 7% по времени (11:01 против 11:48).
Это замер на голосе с длинными паузами — на более быстрых голосах разница между моделями будет уменьшаться.
Какая лучше — зависит от голоса и вкуса, попробуйте обе.

## Предыдущие версии

**v1 (26.09.2026)** — первая версия: спокойная, размеренная книжная подача.
Подача спокойнее и ровнее, чем у v2, но на медленных голосах и длинных фразах
может «тянуть» и затухать к концу куска. Если она вам нравилась больше — она
никуда не делась: файлы в папке [`v1/`](https://huggingface.co/ArtShtorm/Shtorm-PocketTTS-RU/tree/main/v1),
запуск через `v1/config.yaml`.

Токенизатор у v1 и v2 одинаковый.

## Цифры

Замеры **v1**, 7 голосов x 5 сидов, книжный абзац / диалог:

| CER (разборчивость) | UTMOS (качество звука) | обрывы |
|---|---|---|
| 1.6% / 4.0% | 3.64 / 3.52 | 0 из 70 |

## Запуск

```python
from pocket_tts import TTSModel
import scipy.io.wavfile

# fast (по умолчанию):
model = TTSModel.load_model(config="hf://ArtShtorm/Shtorm-PocketTTS-RU/config.yaml")
# slow — спокойная подача:
# model = TTSModel.load_model(config="hf://ArtShtorm/Shtorm-PocketTTS-RU/config_slow.yaml")

voice = model.get_state_for_audio_prompt("my_voice.wav")
audio = model.generate_audio(voice, "Се́рое не́бо висе́ло над го́родом.")
scipy.io.wavfile.write("out.wav", model.sample_rate, audio.numpy())
```

Советы:

- **ударения** — знаком акута (U+0301), как в примере: модель училась на размеченном тексте;
- **реф** — 5 с чистой речи, законченная фраза: модель копирует из него тембр, темп и полосу;
- **куски до ~120-180 знаков**: на длинных громкость к концу проседает;
- **латиница пока не поддерживается** — английские слова и цифры перед синтезом нужно
  нормализовать (записать по-русски). Поддержка латиницы — в планах.

## Ограничения

- паузы на знаках препинания местами длинноваты;
- на длинных кусках — затухание громкости (лечится выравниванием громкости на выходе).

выдачи себя за другого человека, дезинформации и иного вредного или незаконного использования.

# Drama 3 MLX 8-bit

**Built with Fish Audio.**

[Fish Audio Drama 3](https://huggingface.co/fishaudio/drama-3) converted for [mlx-audio](https://github.com/Blaizzy/mlx-audio) on Apple Silicon. This is an unofficial community conversion; Fish Audio did not release or endorse it.

- routed experts: 8-bit, dequantized from the block-FP8 release
- everything else (attention, shared experts, embeddings, audio tower): bf16, as in the reference
- 42 GB on disk, about 49 GB peak memory while generating, so it needs a 64 GB Mac

It sits between [mlx-community/fish-audio-drama-3-4bit](https://huggingface.co/mlx-community/fish-audio-drama-3-4bit) (22 GB) and [mlx-community/fish-audio-drama-3-bf16](https://huggingface.co/mlx-community/fish-audio-drama-3-bf16) (67 GB): only the routed experts are quantized, at 8 bits, so it stays closest to the reference of the quantized options.

## Usage

Drama 3 (`fish_drama3`) is merged into mlx-audio but not yet in a release; until the next release, install from `main`:

```bash
pip install "mlx-audio @ git+https://github.com/Blaizzy/mlx-audio"
```

```python
from mlx_audio.tts.utils import load_model

model = load_model("mlx-community/fish-audio-drama-3-8bit")

for result in model.generate(
    text="<|speaker:0|> Did you hear the news? <|speaker:1|> [sighs] That is a real shame.",
    ref_audio="reference.wav",
    ref_text="Transcript of the reference clip.",
    temperature=1.0,
    top_p=0.9,
):
    print(result.audio.shape)  # 44.1 kHz
```

```bash
python -m mlx_audio.tts.generate --model mlx-community/fish-audio-drama-3-8bit \
    --text "[sighs] Fine. If we miss it, it's on you." \
    --ref_audio reference.wav --ref_text "Transcript of the reference clip." \
    --temperature 1.0 --top_p 0.9 --top_k 30
```

Speaker tags (`<|speaker:0|>` to `<|speaker:15|>`), multiple references and streaming are described in the [model docs](https://github.com/Blaizzy/mlx-audio/blob/main/docs/models/tts/fish-drama3.md).

## Quality and speed

On an M4 Pro (64 GB), voice-cloned from a 24 kHz English reference, checked with Whisper large-v3-turbo:

- a 4-line, 2-speaker dialog: 12/13 seeds correct at temperature 1.0 / top_p 0.9 (the Fish Audio server's defaults) and 10/14 at mlx-audio's default 0.7 / 0.7; the failures skip lines or ramble. That gap is within noise at this sample size, so either setting is fine
- a cue-heavy line (`[sighs] ... [laughs] ...`): 2/3 seeds correct; the failed seed stops after the first sentence. Retry with another seed if a take goes silent
- an English single sentence and a Turkish sentence read correctly
- 42.5 GB after load, 49.1 GB peak while generating a 17.5 s dialog

## Conversion

Made with mlx-audio's converter:

```bash
python -m mlx_audio.tts.models.fish_drama3.convert --src drama-3 --dst drama-3-mlx-8bit \
    --expert-bits 8
```

`NOTICE` lists every change to the original weights.

# VoxCPM2 Arabic Dialects

[VoxCPM2](https://huggingface.co/openbmb/VoxCPM2) with 11 LoRA adapters, one per dialect. A server keeps every
adapter loaded and picks one per request, so one batch can mix dialects. Use it for fast voice cloning in these
dialects; for one model that covers 17 dialects, see
[Teacher-v3](https://huggingface.co/VoxCPM-Kernel/VoxCPM2-Arabic-Teacher-v3).

## At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| Base model | `openbmb/VoxCPM2` (2B parameters, 48 kHz), weights unchanged |
| Trained | 11 LoRA adapters: rank 64, alpha 128, on the attention (q/k/v/o) of the language models and the LocDiT |
| Dialects | 10 Arabic adapters + Hindi-English (table below) |
| Size | 6.55 GB: base 4.96 GB + 145 MB per adapter |
| License | Apache-2.0 |
| Best for | Serving many dialects at once with the [Turbo engine](https://github.com/Speech-Next/voxcpm2-arabic-dialects-turbo) |

## Adapters

| adapter | dialect | training step |
|---|---|---:|
| `ab` | Jordanian (a second Jordanian adapter; its weights differ from `jordanian`) | 67,500 |
| `egyptian` | Egyptian | 49,000 |
| `emirati` | Emirati | 96,000 |
| `hejazi` | Hejazi | 72,000 |
| `hindi_english` | Hindi-English code-switched | 40,500 |
| `iraqi` | Iraqi | 28,000 |
| `jordanian` | Jordanian | 149,000 |
| `najdi` | Najdi | 77,500 |
| `palestinian` | Palestinian | 76,500 |
| `qatari` | Qatari | 53,000 |
| `saudi` | Saudi | 78,000 |

## Files

| path | what it is |
|---|---|
| `model.safetensors`, `audiovae.pth`, `config.json`, tokenizer files | the base VoxCPM2 checkpoint, same weights as `openbmb/VoxCPM2` |
| `adapters/<name>/` | one dialect's LoRA: `lora_weights.safetensors` (fp32) and `lora_config.json` |
| `adapters.json` | index of the adapters: path, description, training step |

## Results

One NVIDIA A10 with the Turbo engine, cloning the 32 voices of
[`VoxCPM-Kernel/Arabic-Hindi-Reference-Voices`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/VoxCPM-Kernel/Arabic-Hindi-Reference-Voices),
each with its own dialect's adapter.

| requests at once | first audio, avg | first audio, p95 | whole sentence, avg |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 24 ms | 26 ms | 0.50 s |
| 16 | 28 ms | 29 ms | 0.46 s |
| 64 | 39 ms | 40 ms | 0.86 s |
| 128 | 64 ms | 66 ms | 1.36 s |
| 200 | 98 ms | 99 ms | 1.94 s |
| 256 | 124 ms | 125 ms | 2.40 s |

| mode | LocDiT steps | first audio p95, 200 requests | CER | WER | UTMOS |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| fast (default) | 2 | 99 ms | 4.6 % | 13.5 % | 2.41 |
| quality (`dit=None`) | 10, with CFG | 277 ms | 4.2 % | 12.5 % | 2.77 |

- **First audio:** time until the first audio chunk is ready. **CER / WER:** character / word error rate of a speech
  recognizer's transcript (better of Whisper large-v3 and Cohere Transcribe Arabic); lower is better.
- **UTMOS:** predicted naturalness, 1-5; higher is better. 6 sentences per voice; the mode table covers the Arabic voices.

## Usage

Install the [Turbo engine](https://github.com/Speech-Next/voxcpm2-arabic-dialects-turbo) (`./setup.sh`), then:

```python
import asyncio
from nanovllm_voxcpm import DialectTTS

async def main():
    tts = await DialectTTS.load("VoxCPM-Kernel/VoxCPM2-Arabic-Dialects")   # fast mode: 2-step distilled LocDiT
    await tts.add_voice("ahmed", "ahmed.wav")
    audio = await tts.synthesize("هلا والله، كيف حالك اليوم؟", dialect="najdi", voice="ahmed")  # 48 kHz
    await tts.close()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

HTTP server (every adapter is registered; a request picks one with `"dialect"`):

# Drama 3 · int4 (hybrid W4A16)

**The smallest working Drama 3.** Unofficial int4 quantization of
[fishaudio/drama-3](https://huggingface.co/fishaudio/drama-3) — Fish Audio's 35B (3B active)
multi-speaker TTS model — with **real eval numbers** and one-command serving through
[SGLang Omni](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni).

Thanks so much to [AK](https://x.com/_akhaliq) for the quantization!

- **22.1 GB** download (vs 41.5 GB original) — routed experts and selected attention projections use int4; the shared expert and audio decoder stay in bf16.
- **Runs on Ampere (A100, sm80)** — GPTQ-Marlin requires compute capability 8.0 or newer.
- Published WER and speaker-similarity evaluations, plus an FP8-vs-int4 comparison on Seed-TTS English.
- 5 verified sample types: plain TTS, voice cloning, `[sighs]`/`[laughs]` tags, long-form, Chinese.

## Samples (all generated by this checkpoint)

| prompt | clip |
|---|---|
| plain TTS | [int4_plain.wav](samples/int4_plain.wav) |
| voice clone (reference clip) | [int4_clone.wav](samples/int4_clone.wav) |
| clone + `[sighs]`/`[laughs]` tags | [int4_tags.wav](samples/int4_tags.wav) |
| long-form | [int4_long.wav](samples/int4_long.wav) |
| Chinese | [int4_zh.wav](samples/int4_zh.wav) |

## Eval

### Seed-TTS English: FP8 vs int4

The two checkpoints were compared on one H200 with the default SGLang Omni server settings:
the 1,088 Seed-TTS English prompts, each cloning the voice of its own reference clip,
sent as non-streaming requests at concurrency 8. WER is computed on the generated audio
transcribed by Qwen3-ASR-1.7B.

| Checkpoint | Weights | Latency mean | Latency p95 | RTF mean | Throughput (req/s) | WER (corpus) | WER without samples above 50% |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `fishaudio/drama-3` (FP8 experts) | 37.0 GB | 1.235 s | 1.902 s | 0.281 | 6.47 | 1.99% | 1.32% |
| `akhaliq/drama-3-int4` | 20.8 GB | 1.334 s | 2.178 s | 0.320 | 5.99 | 1.63% | 1.42% |

*Drama 3 FP8 and int4 checkpoints on Seed-TTS English, concurrency 8, one H200.*

The int4 checkpoint is about 8% slower per request and its WER stays at the FP8 level:
the gap between the two is about as large as the run-to-run spread of one checkpoint
(a second FP8 run measured 1.365 s mean latency and 2.02% WER).

### Community-quant comparison: Whisper large-v3 WER + resemblyzer speaker similarity

An additional evaluation compared this checkpoint against
[darioooooo0o/drama-3-w4a16-32gb](https://huggingface.co/darioooooo0o/drama-3-w4a16-32gb)
(int8 dense layers, targeting 32 GB cards), using the same 8 prompts, the same scorer,
and one A100.

| | mean WER ↓ | mean WER excl. zh¹ ↓ | speaker sim ↑ |
|---|---|---|---|
| **this repo (int4 hybrid, 22.1 GB)** | **0.197** | **0.082** | 0.846 |
| comparison checkpoint (int8 dense, 24.5 GB) | 0.259 | 0.154 | 0.846 |

¹ The Chinese prompt scored WER 1.0 for **both** checkpoints despite nearly identical transcripts —
a jiwer tokenization artifact on unspaced Chinese, not a model difference. Full per-prompt rows in
[`eval/eval_results.json`](eval/eval_results.json); clips in [`eval/`](eval/).

Notable per-prompt outcomes: the comparison checkpoint hallucinated an ending on the long paragraph
(WER 0.667 vs our 0.028); ours truncated the tag line's tail on one take (0.333 vs their 0.25).
Speaker similarity is a tie.

This small-prompt evaluation uses a different dataset and ASR scorer from the Seed-TTS evaluation above;
the WER values should not be compared across the two evaluations.

## Quickstart

Install the current SGLang Omni runtime with Fish Audio support:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni.git
cd sglang-omni

uv venv -p 3.12 .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install --prerelease=allow -e ".[fishaudio]"
```

Download and serve the checkpoint:

```bash
hf download akhaliq/drama-3-int4

sgl-omni serve \
  --model-path akhaliq/drama-3-int4 \
  --port 8000
```

The server reads its quantization from the checkpoint, so it starts with the same command
as the original model. No manual loader patch is required with the current runtime.

Then use the [standard Drama 3 API](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/cookbook/fishaudio_drama3.html):
`/v1/audio/speech` with `input`, optional `references` for voice cloning, `[sighs]`/`[laughs]` tags,
multi-speaker scenes, and `previous_takes` editing all work as on the original.

**Engine weight memory:** 20.8 GB instead of 37.0 GB for the original checkpoint,
which leaves more of the engine's share for the KV cache. This is the engine's weight footprint,
not total serving memory.

An earlier A100-80GB test measured 57.3 GB GPU memory at startup and 57.9 GB peak across
the five sample generations, using explicit memory fractions of
`--tts_engine.gpu_memory_fraction 0.62 --vocoder.gpu_memory_fraction 0.2`.
Those measurements used different settings from the default-server H200 benchmark above.

## What we quantize

| component | original | here | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| text embeddings, output head, router | bf16 | bf16 | retained in bf16 |
| attention `q/k/v/o_proj` of full attention layers | bf16 | **int4** | symmetric 4-bit weights, group size 128 |
| linear attention `in_proj_qkv`, `in_proj_z`, `out_proj` | bf16 | **int4** | symmetric 4-bit weights, group size 128 |
| linear attention `in_proj_a/b` | bf16 | bf16 | retained in bf16 |
| shared-expert MLP | bf16 | **bf16** | int4 passed numerical checks but produced zero audio frames in the earlier serving test; see [`shared_expert_verdict.md`](shared_expert_verdict.md) |
| routed MoE experts (30,720 matrices) | FP8 (block) | **int4** | the bulk: 32.2 GB → 16.6 GB |
| codebook-MTP audio decoder + codec | bf16 | bf16 | retained in bf16 |

The routed MoE experts and quantized attention projections hold symmetric 4-bit weights
with one scale per 128 input channels, and run on GPTQ-Marlin kernels.
GPTQ-Marlin requires compute capability 8.0 or newer.

Quantization method: RTN + per-group clip search (group 128, symmetric), no calibration data.
Weights are stored in GPTQ format; GPTQ storage and kernels do not imply that calibration-based
GPTQ optimization was used.

Reproduce with [`quantize.py`](quantize.py). Quantization statistics are in
[`quant_stats.json`](quant_stats.json).

The repository also retains [`apply_patch.py`](apply_patch.py) for the earlier patched-loader workflow.
That patch fixes fused-name matching (`gate_up_proj`/`qkv_proj`/`in_proj_qkvz`), without which
the earlier loader could silently miss int4 weights and return zero audio frames.
The current SGLang Omni runtime reads the checkpoint's quantization configuration directly.

## Limitations

- **RTN, no calibration** — a GPTQ/AutoRound pass with real calibration data may improve quality; the building blocks are in `quantize.py`.
- Tags prompts occasionally truncate a take — regenerate if needed.
- The 8-prompt community-quant comparison is a small sample; use the larger Seed-TTS evaluation for the reported FP8-vs-int4 comparison.
- Serving has been tested on A100-80GB and H200. Serving on 48 GB and 32 GB cards remains unverified; weight size alone does not establish that the complete serving pipeline fits.

# drama3-small: a compressed Fish Audio Drama 3 that should fit in 12 GB of VRAM

**Built with Fish Audio.** This is a compressed derivative of [Fish Audio Drama 3](https://huggingface.co/fishaudio/drama-3). Fish Audio does not sponsor or endorse it.

drama3-small keeps Drama 3's expressive Japanese and English voice cloning: inline tags, English style directions and director's notes. It should fit in 12 GB of VRAM. The 35B-A3B mixture-of-experts backbone was pruned to 45% of its expert slots and quantized to about 3 bits. It was then distilled back towards the original on Japanese and English speech.

| | |
|---|---|
| File | `drama3-small-IQ3_XXS.gguf`, 9.74 GiB |
| VRAM | Should fit in 12 GB. Measured peak 10.26 GiB (streaming, 30 s reference, RTX 4090); not yet tested on an actual 12 GB card |
| Speed (offline, RTX 4090 / 5090) | About 1.6× / 1.8× real time per request, including reference encoding; about 2.6× / 3.2× once generating |
| Languages | Japanese, English (including Japanese with English technical terms) |
| Features | Zero-shot cloning from about 10–30 s of reference audio; `[tags]`, `<spans>`, English style directions, director's notes |
| Runtime | [audio.cpp](https://github.com/JarodMica/audio.cpp) at `9277495a` + `drama3-small-audiocpp.patch` (CUDA) |

## Samples

All samples come from this GGUF in one take, cloned from a 29-second Japanese reference recording of the repo owner's voice (used with consent).

- **Settings:** temperature 0.7, top-p 0.7, top-k 30, pause fix on (`max_pause_frames` 10).
- **Prompt:** the exact text given to the model, including tags.

| JA inline tags, seed 8010 | `[laughs] まさかそんなオチだとは思わなかった。[sighs] でも、ちょっと安心したよ。` | <audio controls src="https://huggingface.co/pentacoxian-dev/drama3-small-GGUF/resolve/main/samples/ja_laughs_sighs.mp3"></audio> |

Every evening, though, someone in the village swore they could see a faint glow at the top. Nobody ever went to check. Maybe nobody wanted to know.` | <audio controls src="https://huggingface.co/pentacoxian-dev/drama3-small-GGUF/resolve/main/samples/en_story.mp3"></audio> |
| EN mid-line tag, seed 8125 | `I tried everything. [sighs] Nothing works, and I'm out of ideas.` | <audio controls src="https://huggingface.co/pentacoxian-dev/drama3-small-GGUF/resolve/main/samples/en_sighs.mp3"></audio> |

## What changed compared with Drama 3

| Part | Drama 3 | drama3-small |
|---|---|---|
| Routed experts | 256 per layer, FP8 | 256 in layers 0/1/2/36, 100 in the other 36 layers; IQ3_XXS with a speech imatrix (5.20 GiB) |
| Routers / shared experts | n/a | Kept rows; refit layer by layer, then distilled |
| Attention / Gated DeltaNet, embeddings | BF16 | Q8_0 (distilled LoRA merged before quantization) |
| Output head | Full vocabulary | EOS + 4,096 semantic rows (speech only) |
| Audio tower (MTP) | BF16 | Q8_0 |
| Codec | F16 | F16 (unchanged) |

**How expert counts were chosen:**
- Experts were ranked by routing mass on stratified Japanese and English speech: plain, technical code-switching, styled, and tagged.
- Per-layer counts follow measured sensitivity. Pruning layer 0, 1, 2 or 36 costs far more than any other layer, so those four keep all 256. That reallocation alone cut the proxy KL by 26% compared with a uniform 116 experts per layer.

**Recovery:**
- A layerwise refit of routers and shared experts.
- Then 100 steps of knowledge distillation from the exact FP8 model, using KL on the semantic and audio-tower distributions.
- Data: about 282 h of real speech plus 5,501 lines read by the original model (tags, directions, technical Japanese).
- Longer distillation lowered the proxy KL further but made free-running generation worse: dropped content after the first sentence. The released checkpoint was chosen by listening tests.

## Evaluation

**Proxy fidelity.** Teacher-forced KL against the FP8 original, over 4,097 speech candidates, on 152 held-out Japanese and English pairs. Lower is better.

| Model | Size | KL |
|---|---|---|
| Drama 3, all experts at Q4_K | 16.9 GiB | 0.013 |
| Community Q2_K package | 9.8 GiB | 0.094 |
| drama3-small before distillation | 9.74 GiB | 0.0997 |
| **drama3-small (this release)** | **9.74 GiB** | **0.0735** |

**Listening tests.** 58 varied lines, one take each: long-form, numbers, technical terms, every emotion direction and tag, 7 voices. A take counts as a failure if it runs on, drops content, or comes out in the wrong voice (Whisper large-v3-turbo CER/WER and WavLM speaker similarity).

| Model | Failures | Speaker similarity |
|---|---|---|
| Drama 3, FP8 original (PyTorch) | 7 / 58 | 0.911 |
| drama3-small, no pause fix | 10 / 58 | 0.910 |
| **drama3-small + pause fix** | **0 / 58** | **0.947** |

Across 172 takes in five listening sets, the pause fix reduced failures from 30 to 1, and the remaining one is a mispronunciation. Runaways went from 28 to 0, and the longest in-sentence pause from 35 s to 3.5 s. Error rates on clean takes and average durations are unchanged. Most of the remaining failures without the fix are shared with the original model.

## Speed

Measured with `audiocpp_server` and the model already loaded:
- Pause fix on; temperature 0.7, top-p 0.7, top-k 30.
- Each request also encodes the 29 s reference clip.
- 4 lines (JA short, JA long, EN, JA with tags) × 2–3 seeds.

Real time = seconds of audio per second of wall time.

| GPU | Mode | Time to first audio | Overall | Long line (13–14 s of audio) | Steady generation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RTX 4090 (24 GB) | offline | n/a | 1.6× | 2.0× | about 57 frames/s (2.6×) |
| RTX 5090 (32 GB) | offline | n/a | 1.8× | 2.2× | about 69 frames/s (3.2×) |
| RTX 4090 (24 GB) | streaming | 1.9 s | 1.5× | 1.8× | |
| RTX 5090 (32 GB) | streaming | 1.8 s | 1.7× | 2.1× | |
| ZeroGPU (RTX PRO 6000) | offline, CLI per request | n/a | 9–14 s per request end to end; the 10.5 GB model loads on every request | | |

- Each request has a fixed cost of about 1.5–2 s: encoding the reference plus processing the prompt. That is why very short lines run at about 1× real time.
- Shorter references make that cost smaller.
- Speed on 12 GB cards (for example an RTX 4070) has not been measured yet; expect it to be lower.

## Usage

Build the patched audio.cpp:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/JarodMica/audio.cpp && cd audio.cpp
git checkout 9277495a
git apply /path/to/drama3-small-audiocpp.patch
scripts/build_linux.sh --cuda on --models fish_drama3
```

Clone a voice from the command line (`requests.json` holds `{"requests": [{"id", "text", "voice_ref", "options": {"reference_text": ...}, "seed", "temperature": 0.7, "top_k": 30, "top_p": 0.7, "max_tokens": 645}]}`):

```bash
AUDIOCPP_DRAMA3_MAX_PAUSE_FRAMES=10 AUDIOCPP_DRAMA3_SILENCE_CODES=silence_codes.json \
build/linux-cuda-release/bin/audiocpp_cli --task clon --family fish_drama3 --backend cuda --mode offline \
  --model drama3-small-IQ3_XXS.gguf --request-sequence requests.json --out-dir out \
  --session-option fish_drama3.cpu_expert_layers=0 --session-option fish_drama3.context_length=4096
```

Or run `audiocpp_server` with a model entry `{"id": "drama3-small", "family": "fish_drama3", "task": "clon", "path": "drama3-small-IQ3_XXS.gguf", "voice_presets": {...}}` and call `POST /v1/audio/speech` with `{"model": "drama3-small", "input": "...", "voice": "<preset>", "options": {"max_pause_frames": "10", "silence_codes": "silence_codes.json"}}`.

Recommended sampling: temperature 0.7, top-p 0.7, top-k 30.

### Pause fix (recommended)

Drama 3, and more often its compressed versions, sometimes goes silent at a tag or sentence boundary and never resumes or stops. The patch adds a sampler-side fix, controlled by request options or `AUDIOCPP_DRAMA3_*` environment variables:

- **`max_pause_frames`** (10 is 0.47 s; 21.5 frames is 1 s): after this many consecutive silent frames, the silence codes in **`silence_codes`** (this repo's `silence_codes.json`, 143 codes) are masked out of the next draw. The model must resume speaking or end.
- **Length guard:** the expected length is estimated from the text. A pause after `pause_end_ratio` (2.0) times that length ends the take, and `pause_cap_ratio` (3.0) times stops it regardless. This prevents the model from babbling when it is forced to continue past the end.

## Limitations

- **Requires the patched audio.cpp:** IQ quant types, per-layer expert counts, the speech-only head and the pause fix are not in upstream audio.cpp or llama.cpp.
- **12 GB is an estimate from measurements on 24–32 GB cards, not a test on a 12 GB card.** Offline-mode VRAM also grows with output length: 10.65 GiB for a short line, 13–15 GiB for 30–40 s outputs. On 12 GB cards, use streaming mode, or keep `max_tokens` around 645 (30 s).
- **Weaknesses shared with the original model:**
  - `[gasps]` at the start of a line
  - `<slow>…</slow>` spans
  - phone numbers, e-mail addresses and codes like "UA 837"; write these out as words
  - some English technical terms read in Japanese (for example "Kubernetes")
- **When the model loses its place mid-line,** the pause fix ends the take cleanly, but the rest of that line is skipped.
